_doc: Stream E (play-test 4, S19: 'an indicator above the name showing what they are — merchant type, barber, skill reset…; names are random/pointless, some just Townsfolk'). The line drawn ABOVE a non-player character's name (stream A sends it as `info.title`; js/sim/npc-names.js reads this file). `shops` = the title for an NPC who keeps that data/provinces/shops.json kind (wins over the role, so the smith reads 'Weaponsmith'); `roles` = the title for an NPC's schedules/offices/vignette role; an NPC with no role takes the trade from its name ('Cadoc the pedlar' -> 'Pedlar', 'Nell Pike, eel-catcher' -> 'Eel-catcher'), else `fallback`. `placeholders` = names that are only a job (lower case): a non-quest NPC called one of these (or its own role) is given a real name from data/names/torbor.json, seeded by the NPC's key so it keeps it across restarts. Service NPCs say what they do after a dash, so the player knows who resets talents without asking.

titled._doc: W27 (owner feedback 8, report #48: "only show titles for NPCs the player interacts with, intentionally placed for the player to find; not random NPC fillers like woodcutter"). WHO SHOWS A TITLE. Stream A sends `info.title` only when this says yes, in this order: (1) the NPC record's own `titled` flag (every record stream E writes carries one: quest files' npcs, offices.json offices and set-piece NPCs, travellers / wanderers crew entries and folk, road-events NPCs, the guard / carter / angler rows of <zone>.quest.json); (2) `types[<placement type>]` for a placement row without the flag (the main placement files, which only B's re-bake may rewrite): an `npc` row is a quest NPC -> true, a `folk` row is filler -> false; (3) a quest NPC id listed in data/quests/marks/givers.json -> its `titled`; (4) `roles[<role>]`; (5) `default`. A filler NPC keeps its real name and shows nothing above it. MADE by tools/content-givers.mjs from tools/content-titled.mjs.
